newsitem.title: UK: UK bookmakers cut odds on Labour election victory.
newsitem.headline: UK bookmakers cut odds on Labour election victory.

text.p: Bookmakers William Hill cut the odds on the opposition Labour party winning the May 1 election to 1-5 from 2-9 on Thursday after new polls suggested the party was still well ahead of the ruling Conservatives.

Spokesman Graham Sharpe said the firm was predicting an overall Labour majority of between 71 and 79 seats and had lengthened the odds on a Conservative win to 13-2 from 6-1. The odds on a hung parliament stay at 9-2.
"Cash for a Labour victory is now rolling in," Sharpe said in a statement.
The odds on a Conservative win shortened on Wednesday after a poll showed the party just five points behind Labour but the latest three soundings put the opposition between 19 and 21 points ahead.
The odds on Labour winning the most seats dropped to 1-7 from 1-6 while the Conservatives' chances of pulling off the same feat lengthened to 4-1 from 7-2.
